content: 1. Grapefruit consumption can increase the plasma levels or effects of doxorubicin liposomal by interfering with the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. It is recommended to exercise caution and closely monitor the patient during coadministration. 2. Grapefruit can elevate the levels or effects of dronabinol by altering CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Dronabinol is a substrate of CYP3A4. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 3. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of dronedarone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative medications should be considered. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 4. Grapefruit may increase the levels or effects of dutasteride by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 5. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of duvelisib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. When coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the duvelisib dose to 15 mg twice daily to mitigate toxicity risks. 6. Grapefruit elevates the levels or effects of edoxaban by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. Dose adjustments may be required when coadministered with strong P-gp inhibitors. For DVT/PE treatment, reduce the dose to 30 mg orally once daily. No dose reduction is recommended for NVAF. 7. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 8. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of elacestrant by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. 9. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of elagolix by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. 10. Grapefruit elevates the levels or effects of eletriptan by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and closely monitor the patient. 11. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of eliglustat by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors are contraindicated in poor or intermediate metabolizers of eliglustat. For extensive metabolizers, reduce the eliglustat dose from 84 mg twice daily to 84 mg once daily. Eliglustat is contraindicated if strong or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors are coadministered with strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 12. Grapefruit increases the levels of elvitegravir by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and closely monitor the patient. Elvitegravir is a CYP3A4 substrate, and coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may further elevate its levels. 13. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of encorafenib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose to one-third of the original dose (e.g., from 450 mg/day to 150 mg/day). After discontinuing the inhibitor for 3–5 elimination half-lives, resume the previous encorafenib dose. 14. Grapefruit increases the toxicity of enfortumab vedotin by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. Enfortumab vedotin is an antibody-drug conjugate that releases monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE) via proteolytic cleavage. MMAE is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4 in vitro. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase free MMAE exposure, leading to higher toxicity risks. 15. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of entrectinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit products when taking entrectinib, a CYP3A4 substrate. 16. Grapefruit elevates the levels or effects of eplerenone by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and closely monitor the patient for hyperkalemia. 17. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of erdafitinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, closely monitor for adverse reactions and consider dose reductions. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the erdafitinib dose in the absence of drug-related toxicities. 18. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of ergotamine by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. 19. Grapefruit elevates the levels or effects of erlotinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and closely monitor the patient. 20. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of erythromycin base, erythromycin ethylsuccinate, erythromycin lactobionate, and erythromycin stearate by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. 21. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of estradiol, estradiol vaginal, conjugated synthetic estrogens, esterified estrogens, and estropipate by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and closely monitor the patient. Coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations of estrogens and associated toxicities. 22. Grapefruit elevates the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and etonogestrel by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and closely monitor the patient. 23. Grapefruit may increase the levels or effects of etoposide by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 24. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of etravirine by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and closely monitor the patient. 25. Grapefruit may increase the levels or effects of eucalyptus by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 26. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of everolimus by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. 27. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of fedratinib by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the fedratinib dose to 200 mg/day. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, increase the fedratinib dose to 300 mg/day for 2 weeks, then to 400 mg/day as tolerated. 28. Grapefruit elevates the levels or effects of felodipine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and closely monitor the patient. 29. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of fentanyl (including intranasal, transdermal, and transmucosal formulations) by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors is necessary, monitor patients for respiratory depression and sedation at frequent intervals and consider fentanyl dose adjustments until stable drug effects are achieved. 30. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of fesoterodine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and closely monitor the patient. 31. Grapefruit decreases the levels or effects of fexinidazole by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor fexinidazole for decreased efficacy due to reduced plasma concentrations of active M1 and M2 metabolites. 32. Grapefruit decreases the levels or effects of fexofenadine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This interaction is contraindicated. Coadministration with grapefruit, apple, or orange juice reduces fexofenadine bioavailability by inhibiting P-gp. Separate administration by at least 4 hours. 33. Grapefruit may increase the levels or effects of finasteride by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 34. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of finerenone by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. 35. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. Coadministration of flibanserin with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated due to the risk of severe hypotension or syncope. 36. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of fludrocortisone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and closely monitor the patient. 37. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of fluticasone furoate and fluticasone inhaled by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and closely monitor the patient. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to fluticasone. 38. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of fluvoxamine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and closely monitor the patient. 39. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and closely monitor the patient. 40. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and closely monitor the patient. 41. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of fostamatinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to R406 (the major active metabolite of fostamatinib). Monitor for toxicities that may require dose reduction. 42. Grapefruit may increase the levels or effects of ganaxolone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. Changes in ganaxolone exposure when coadministered with strong, moderate, or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors are not expected to be clinically significant. 43. Grapefruit increases the levels of gefitinib by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Coadministration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of gefitinib-related adverse effects. 44. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of gepirone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. 45. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of gilteritinib by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, closely monitor for gilteritinib-related adverse effects. Interrupt and reduce gilteritinib dosage in patients with serious or life-threatening toxicity. 46. Grapefruit significantly increases the levels or effects of glasdegib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. Consider alternative therapies that are not strong CYP3A inhibitors or monitor for increased risk of adverse effects, including QTc interval prolongation. 47. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and closely monitor the patient. 48. Grapefruit may increase the levels or effects of green tea by mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. This food-drug interaction might potentiate the clinical effects and duration of action of caffeine. 49. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of guanfacine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations.
